problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above.
Find the unknown function $f(t)$ in the general solution to the system, shown below.

$$
\text{x}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}f(t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}
$$

*Hint: One of the eigenvalues of the matrix is ${\lambda }_{1}=1+2\text{i}.$*
worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ 

We are given that the eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=1+2\text{i}.$ 

Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors. For ${\lambda }_{1}=1+2\text{i},$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}-2\text{i} & -4 \\ 1 & -2\text{i}\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2\text{i} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}$ is 
${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=1+2\text{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{(1+2\text{i})t}.
$$

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{(1+2\text{i})t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\text{i}(2{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)) \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\text{i}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]{e}^{t} \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${w}_{1}$ and ${w}_{2}$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $f(t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).$
